'''Johnny Steven Rodgers''' (born July 5, 1951) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player.  He played [[college football]] for the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska Cornhuskers]] and won the [[Heisman Trophy]] in 1972.  Rodgers played in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) with the [[Montreal Alouettes]] and in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[San Diego Chargers]].  He was inducted into the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 2000.

'''Johnny Lyndell Hector''' (born November 26, 1960) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player for 10 seasons the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M Aggies]] and was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the second round of the [[1983 NFL draft]]. Standing {{height|ft=5|in=11}} and 200 lbs., Hector played Jets from 1983 to 1992. His best season as a pro came during the 1987 season when he was tied with [[Charles White (American football)|Charles White]] for most rushing [[touchdown]]s in the league with 11. During the mid to late 1980s, he served as a member of the 'Two-Headed Monster' backfield along with [[Freeman McNeil]], creating a one-two punch at running back among the most potent in the league.

Hector compiled 4,280 rushing yards on 1,051 carries and 41 touchdowns; he also caught 188 passes for 1,661 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gehman |first1=Jim |title=Where Are They Now: Johnny Hector |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/where-are-they-now-johnny-hector |website=New York Jets |access-date=November 2, 2020 |date=May 9, 2019}}</ref>  His last NFL touchdown was against the [[New England Patriots]] on December 23, 1990.

He played high school football at [[New Iberia Senior High School]] in [[New Iberia, Louisiana]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Partsch III |first=Raymond |title=From small town to the Big Apple, Hector didn’t change |url=https://www.thedailyiberian.com/sports/from-small-town-to-the-big-apple-hector-didn-t-change/article_b3dd82e2-8cfe-11ea-819e-c378def58be4.html |access-date=2023-05-11 |website=[[The Daily Iberian]] |language=en}}</ref> and graduated in 1979. He lives in Lafayette, Louisiana with his wife, Karla.

'''Johnny Lee Rembert''' (born January 19, 1961)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Johnny Rembert Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RembJo00.htm |access-date=November 16, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for 10 seasons with the [[New England Patriots]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]]. Rembert was a member of the 1985 AFC champions who played the [[Chicago Bears]] in [[Super Bowl XX]] in New Orleans.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1985 New England Patriots Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nwe/1985.htm |access-date=November 17, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the Wild Card Round of the 1985–86 NFL playoffs, he had a fumble recovery return for a touchdown against the New York Jets.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - New England Patriots at New York Jets - December 28th, 1985 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/198512280nyj.htm |access-date=November 17, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was selected to the AFC [[Pro Bowl]] team twice (1988 and 1989).<ref>{{Cite web |title=1988 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1988/probowl.htm |access-date=November 17, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=1989 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1989/probowl.htm |access-date=November 17, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He won AFC Defensive Player of the Week in Week 10 of the 1988 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1988 NFL Week 10 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1988/week_10.htm |access-date=November 17, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

After his playing career, Rembert was the director of athletics at [[Edward Waters College]] in [[Jacksonville, Florida]] and also the quality control representative for the NFL.<ref name="y523">{{cite web | last=Goode | first=Jon| title=Catching up with Johnny Rembert | website=SouthCoastToday.com | date=2005-01-16 | url=https://www.southcoasttoday.com/story/sports/2005/01/16/catching-up-with-johnny-rembert/50320479007/ | access-date=2025-04-29}}</ref>
